title: Intermittent 'No data' dashboard tiles & tracing gaps during high-load tenant bursts
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported dashboards showing intermittent 'No data' tiles during peak traffic windows while traces showed gaps for the same time ranges. Impacted tenants span Hosted and Dedicated deployments. This is causing repeated customer escalations and confusion during on-call triage.

Observed behavior:
- Dashboard tiles for some tenant metric panels display 'No data' for short windows (30s—3m) around traffic bursts while underlying raw events exist in logs.
- Traces for the same request IDs are sometimes missing spans or have discontinuities that align with the metric drop windows.
- Downstream alerting missed for 3 customers during last 48 hours due to metric tombstoning.

Hypothesis: A coordinated failure across the ingest pipeline where short-lived ingestion shard evictions (due to autoscale/rebalance) plus aggressive metric tombstone TTLs cause windows of query-materialization gaps. Additionally, trace stitcher sampling windows appear misaligned with the metric ingestion watermark, leading to gaps in trace linking.

Repro steps:
1) Run a tenant-specific synthetic load generator (loadgen/tenant-burst) with a sustained 4x baseline QPS for 5 minutes.
2) Observe metrics ingestion pipeline (ingest-proxy -> shard-kv -> compactor) for eviction logs.
3) Query dashboards for the tenant window and inspect traces for same request IDs.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Temporarily increased tombstone grace TTL for affected tenant shards from 30s -> 180s (hotfix applied to staging and rolled to two impacted Dedicated clusters).
- Enabled a conservative sampling fallback in trace stitcher to prefer trace continuity over strict sampling thresholds.

Action plan (this ticket):
- Root-cause analysis: add additional telemetry and tight logging around shard rebalances, compaction, and tombstone pruning logic (ETA 2d).
- Implement deterministic backoff on shard eviction during high-ingest windows to avoid mass evictions (design then implementation, ETA 1 sprint).
- Adjust default tombstone/grace windows and make them tenant-configurable with sensible safe defaults (P1 follow-up).
- Add an observability runbook entry and alert that correlates sudden per-tenant metric drop with shard eviction events so on-call can triage faster.
- Roll a canary patch to Hosted and Dedicated with staggered rollout and monitoring (post-PR review).

Success criteria:
- No more unexplained 'No data' tiles for >72h post-release during synthetic stress tests and a week of real traffic.
- Trace continuity for previously failing request chains is restored.
- Customer escalations for this symptom reduced to zero for affected accounts within 7 days of release.
